original.title: Saturated private-history handover and a jump of at least 2k
original.statement: At the rightmost old fresh host in a record row with k fresh labels, its entire strict postbirth private history is permuted into the current right tail. Every matched historical value is at most T−k; if the host has a previous postbirth row, its current column jump is at least 2k.
assumptions: Canonical record row and rightmost old fresh host. C19 age≥17 consequence requires the named C19 hypothesis, which must not be folded into unconditional statement.

exactAuditedStatement: For record rowq>=1 with k=d(q)-T(q)-1>=1, let c*<q be rightmost old fresh host. Then {f(a, c*):c*<a<q}={f(q, r):c*<r<q}, both sets with q-c*-1 distinct labels, each<=T-k. If c*<=q-2, f(q, c*)-f(q-1, c*)>=2k.
hypotheses: Full canonical journals; fresh means value>T(q).
C19 age>=17 corollary is separately conditional and not part of unconditional statement.
proofDependencyMap: Shared canonical foundation: exact positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and P01-P12, independently reconstructed in ../CANONICAL-FOUNDATIONS.md with exact declaration mapping and game interpretation. DEPENDENCIES.json records the additional service lemmas. Final kernel receipts bind the source versions.
Journal identity, P14 inversion-journal fact derived by MEX, P16 journal ceiling derived by row max, fresh-label coverage derived by P11.
independentDerivationAndChecks: Fresh labels T+1,..., d-1 all occur by P11 and cannot belong to old journals. Two fresh hosts in physical order cannot decline: MEX would place the later fresh value in the earlier journal<=T. Thus c* holds T+k and all strict right tail cells are<=T.

For any tail valuex and any fresh hostc<r, MEX forces x into that journal. It cannot be a seed d(i), i<c, or own birth d(c), because current column r>c cannot emit any earlier diagonal. Therefore x was privately served at some c<a<q with d(a)>x.
Different fresh hosts for fixed x have distinct source rows by row injectivity. Therefore k<=#{a<q:d(a)>x}<=T-x, giving x<=T-k.

At fixed c*, the distinct q-c*-1 tail values map into the equally many postbirth rows(c*, q). They cannot share one source row because one cell has one value. Thus bijection onto all rows and all postbirth values distinct; no historical row is omitted. Birth row excluded essentially.

If previous postbirth row exists, its value<=T-k while current is T+k, giving jump>=2k. If c*=q-1, history and tail are empty and jump corollary is inapplicable. Nothing bounds positive column jumps or proves NoTriple.
